title: BDK Project Settings
description: Project-level configuration for the Broneq Dev Kit (.bdk/settings.json)

languages.description: Languages and frameworks detected in this project. Free-form: an entry only needs a matching rules/languages/<name>.md (shipped or user-supplied) to inject anything. See .claude/rules/language-rules.md.

test-tools.description: Commands to run the test suite, one entry per tier. Give every entry a `tier` (fast | e2e) and a `scoped` template so callers can run only what changed; `command` is the full-suite form and runs once, at the end of a plan.

lint-tools.description: Commands to run linters/formatters/typecheckers, one entry per tier (lint | format | typecheck). Give lint/format entries a `scoped` template and typecheckers an `incremental` form so per-group checks do not re-analyse the whole project.

lavish.description: Route bundled multi-question decision points through the lavish-axi binary instead of terminal AskUserQuestion. Also requires the binary on PATH; skills check both and fall back silently when either is absent.

quality.description: Per-category overrides for BDK's language-agnostic rules in rules/<name>.md. Read by scripts/inject-rules.py. Keys are rule names (code-quality, architecture, design-patterns, security, engineering-judgment, test-quality).

language-rules.description: Per-language overrides for rules/languages/<lang>.md. Read by scripts/inject-language-rules.py. Keys are entries from `languages`.

ruleOverride.description: Either a bare path to the override file, or an object choosing how it combines with the BDK default.

path.description: Path to the override file, relative to project root

mode.description: extends appends the override to the BDK default; replace discards the default

type.description: The runner or framework this entry invokes (vitest, playwright, pytest, eslint, tsc, go-test, …). Free-form: it names the tool, and BDK reads it to infer a missing `tier`, so a framework name is more useful here than a package manager name.

tier.description: Which class of check this is. test-tools use fast | e2e; lint-tools use lint | format | typecheck. Omitted → BDK infers it from `type`/`command`, which is a guess: declare it. The tier decides when the command may run — a `fast` tier runs per group, an `e2e` tier only at the end of a plan (or scoped to specs the group itself touched).

command.description: Full, unscoped shell command — the whole suite or the whole project. The slowest form: reserved for the one end-of-plan gate.

scoped.description: Command scoped to an explicit path list. Must contain the `{files}` placeholder, which the caller replaces with space-separated paths (e.g. `npx vitest run {files}`, `npx eslint {files}`).

related.description: Command that runs the tests *covering* the given source files, for runners that can compute that themselves (e.g. `npx vitest related --run {files}`). Must contain `{files}`. Replaces asking an agent which tests cover a change.

failed.description: Command that re-runs only the previously failing tests (e.g. `npx vitest run --changed`, `npx playwright test --last-failed`). Used by fix cycles so a fix attempt does not pay for a full suite.

incremental.description: Cache-reusing form of a whole-project check that cannot be scoped to a file list — typecheckers above all (e.g. `tsc -b --incremental`). Preferred over `command` for repeated per-group runs in one worktree.
